lessons.title: Text files, modes and paths
lessons.prepare: Python editor, a dedicated disposable practice folder and a text editor. Keep original class data separate.

slides.title: Text files, modes and paths
slides.notes: Success means choose read/write/append deliberately, explain relative paths and preserve one record per line. Use only disposable practice files when demonstrating write mode.
body: Unit 1 · Week 7 · Lesson 1
Save records and read them in a later run.

slides.title: Retrieval: keeping values
slides.notes: Allow one minute without notes then compare. A list retains values while that program is running; a saved text file can be read in a later run. Traversal visits each item. Ask what information must persist beyond program exit before naming the file format.
body: What does a list retain during a program run?
What could preserve records after the program exits?
What does sequential traversal mean?
Compare your explanation with a partner.

slides.title: Three file modes
slides.notes: Read r requires an existing file. Write w creates a missing file or truncates an existing file when opened. Append a creates a missing file or adds at its end. Use an existing practice file containing 2, then ask what w and a would do before executing. with closes the file when its block exits, including after an exception.

slides.title: A path starts from a location
slides.notes: Explain a relative name is resolved from current working directory, which can differ from script location. Demonstrate the actual school editor setting and locate the practice folder. An absolute path specifies its full location; avoid machine-specific paths in shared examples. Learners point to their folder without editing important files. Missing file in r raises FileNotFoundError.
body: A path identifies a file’s location.
"practice.txt" is relative to the working directory.
The script folder and working directory can differ.
Locate your disposable practice folder before running.

slides.title: Two records, two lines
slides.notes: In the practice folder, w writes 2 followed by newline, then a writes 5 followed by newline. The file contains two records, 2 and 5, not 25. UTF-8 makes text encoding explicit. Predict first, run, inspect with a text editor. Re-running the whole snippet resets the file first because w comes before a; running only append again adds another 5. Emphasise both cases.
body: Predict the file contents before running.
What changes if only the append block runs again?
slides.code:
with open("practice.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    file.write("2\n")
with open("practice.txt", "a", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    file.write("5\n")

slides.title: Reading the records in order
slides.notes: Expected displayed lines 2 and 5, with a third 5 if only append ran again. strip removes surrounding whitespace, including newline, from the string. Driver runs a read; navigator compares actual file contents, then swap and append 0 before reading again. Support: provide with header. Stretch: explain why a file with no final newline can join a later append onto the last record.
body: Read and compare with the text editor.
Append a new record, then read again.

slides.title: Which mode preserves earlier records?
slides.notes: Correct C:a. w replaces old text and r does not permit writing. Collect simultaneous choices then explain. If several choose w, compare opening w with opening a on two disposable copies. File mode choice matters before any write call.
body: You need to retain old records and add one at the end.
A: r     B: w     C: a
Choose alone and justify your choice.
Why must the newline convention stay consistent?

slides.title: Exit ticket: explain the file contract
slides.notes: Expected one non-negative integer per line, consistent UTF-8, newline after each record, a to add and r to read. A relative file path uses working directory. Collect individual explanations; use errors for a short mode/path reminder before validation.
body: State a format for one quantity per line.
Choose modes for adding and reading records.
Explain what w does to an existing file.
Where does a relative path begin?

lessons.title: Conversion, range and retry
lessons.prepare: Python editor and a response/test table. Use whole-number quantities of zero or more.

slides.title: Conversion, range and retry
slides.notes: Success means distinguish conversion failure from range failure, catch expected ValueError and retry until a suitable quantity is entered. Validation checks rules, not whether a plausible value is truthful.
body: Unit 1 · Week 7 · Lesson 2
Convert input, check its value and respond clearly.

slides.title: Retrieval: text becoming a number
slides.notes: Expected input returns str. int("12") succeeds; int("2.5") and int("three") raise ValueError. int("-3") succeeds as conversion but violates a non-negative quantity rule. Ask learners to commit before comparing.
body: What type does input() return?
Predict int("12") and int("2.5").
Does int("-3") satisfy a non-negative quantity rule?
Compare conversion and range in your explanation.

slides.title: Different reasons to reject input
slides.notes: Students classify individually, compare in pairs then justify. "0" and "12" convert and satisfy range. "-3" converts but fails range. "three" and "2.5" fail integer-text conversion. Accept zero explicitly. Support: two stages on paper. Stretch: explain why conversion alone is insufficient.

slides.title: Catching a specific conversion error
slides.notes: With input three, int raises ValueError, so message prints. With 12, conversion succeeds and except does not run. Catch the expected error rather than bare except. This isolated fragment demonstrates conversion only: it does not yet retry or check range. Do not use quantity after failed conversion without a successful retry.
body: Predict for inputs three and 12.
Which expected error does this handler catch?

slides.title: A separate range check
slides.notes: This fragment assumes conversion already succeeded. With-3 it prints Quantity cannot be negative. With 0 it prints Accepted:0. With 12 accepted 12. Learners change the literal, predict and run. A value can be the right type but outside the allowed range. Avoid claiming this literal example handles arbitrary input by itself.
body: Predict again with quantity = 0.
Why does a successful conversion still need this check?

slides.title: A retry loop combines the checks
slides.notes: Trace inputs three, then-3, then 0. First ValueError prints whole-number message. Second converts but prints negative message. Third passes >=0 and break leaves the loop with quantity 0. while True makes retry explicit; break exits only after suitable input. Swap driver/navigator for 2.5 then 4. Catch ValueError specifically. Support: trace conversion, range and action columns.
body: Trace three, then -3, then 0.
When does break allow the program to continue?

slides.title: Does valid mean truthful?
slides.notes: Correct B: accepted 12 fits the declared type/range but could still be a wrong real-world quantity. Validation does not establish truth. Collect responses before discussion. Ask for a value that is plausible but mistyped, then contrast conversion/range rejection.
body: The program accepts a quantity of 12.
“This proves the user entered the true quantity.”
A: agree     B: disagree
Choose and explain what the checks actually establish.

slides.title: Exit ticket: choose useful input tests
slides.notes: Expected zero accepted, -1 range rejected, textword and decimal text conversion rejected, ordinary integer accepted. Handler ValueError. Explain retry with an unsuitable value followed by a suitable one. Use answers to decide conversion/range support before file processing.
body: Give tests for zero, a negative and unsuitable text.
State the expected response to each.
Name the exception for invalid integer text.
Explain why a retry test needs a later suitable input.

lessons.title: Combine game tests with reading and appending results
lessons.prepare: Before class verify the nominated editor uses a school-approved Python/Pygame installation. Extract the whole pygame-teaching-pack.zip into a writable disposable folder. Open https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/index.html#y11-4 and workbook.md, faded_practice.py, practice-tests.csv and readiness.csv. Run python lab_runner.py 4. Use supplied named state/runner infrastructure; no student-authored classes, paid media or assessed project code. Record device, interpreter and support. Paper traces support reasoning; live window/keyboard evidence remains necessary. The suggested 55-minute allocation is untrialled; use the supplied 50-minute adaptation when required.

slides.title: Test the game and preserve its history
body: Unit 1 · Week 7 · Lesson 3
Read valid scores and append one finished result.
slides.notes: Run python lab_runner.py 4 in a disposable extracted folder. The worked lab accepts integer history scores0..2; the changed lab accepts0,2,4,6. Success: distinguish missing/empty/malformed data, append once after finished, show a visible failed write and retry, and retain pause/reset/timeout evidence. Stage4 uses the same two-station lab; Week7 Lesson4 controlled practical stays unchanged. Teaching lab and matching workbook: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/index.html#y11-4; https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/workbook.md. Worked files and changed scaffold are public formative resources. Relevant Pygame references: https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/event.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/time.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/rect.html .

slides.title: Retrieve modes and validation
body: Which mode preserves earlier scores: a or w?
How does a missing file differ from an empty one?
Does int conversion alone enforce a score range?
slides.notes: Append a retains prior text; w truncates an existing file. An empty file opens and traverses zero records; missing raises FileNotFoundError unless handled. int("3") converts but3 is invalid for the worked0..2 score policy. Missing history is intentionally treated as no previous scores here; it is a stated lab policy, not a universal rule. Teaching lab and matching workbook: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/index.html#y11-4; https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/workbook.md. Worked files and changed scaffold are public formative resources. Relevant Pygame references: https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/event.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/time.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/rect.html .

slides.title: Read each score and check its domain
body: The complete loader returns scores and warnings.
slides.notes: Excerpt from rules.load_history; the omitted surrounding try handles missing as empty and other read/encoding errors with a warning. int strips/converts, then the domain check rejects out-of-range integers. Worked policy accepts0,1,2. Malformed or out-of-range lines are skipped with their line number in warnings; valid later lines are still processed. Model a file containing 2,three,1,9: valid[2,1], warnings for lines2 and4. Empty and missing both yield[] with no warnings under this lab policy. Do not reuse the previous chapter’s whole-file-rejection policy without stating the difference. Teaching lab and matching workbook: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/index.html#y11-4; https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/workbook.md. Worked files and changed scaffold are public formative resources. Relevant Pygame references: https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/event.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/time.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/rect.html .
slides.strategy: Teacher model and worked record trace

slides.title: Append only after a successful finish
body: Predict repeated calls for the same finished state.
slides.notes: Focused success-path excerpt of save_result. The complete supplied function wraps the open/write in try/except OSError and returns a visible Not saved message while leaving saved=False. Only after the with block succeeds is saved=True. The runner attempts automatically once when finished and S explicitly retries a failed write. Reset creates a fresh unsaved state for the next run while keeping old file records. Test full supplied function, not this excerpt alone. Teaching lab and matching workbook: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/index.html#y11-4; https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/workbook.md. Worked files and changed scaffold are public formative resources. Relevant Pygame references: https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/event.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/time.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/rect.html .
slides.strategy: Predict, model and inspect file state
slides.code:
if state["mode"] != "finished" or state["saved"]:
    return ""
with Path(path).open("a", encoding="utf-8") as target:
    target.write(str(state["score"]) + "\n")
state["saved"] = True

slides.title: Specify expected results before testing
slides.notes: Model pause and timeout with rule tests, then observe live transitions in the runner. Paused95000 ms update leaves x and remaining unchanged. Starting/resuming/resetting discards that frame’s delta. An update with remaining50 and dt50 finishes with remaining0 before movement/collection, so an overlapping station earns no late point. Two successful saves on the same finished state append one row. A failed target (use an existing disposable directory as the path) returns Not saved and leaves saved=False; retry with a writable file. Never change real school permissions to simulate failure. Teaching lab and matching workbook: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/index.html#y11-4; https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/workbook.md. Worked files and changed scaffold are public formative resources. Relevant Pygame references: https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/event.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/time.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/rect.html .
slides.strategy: Guided test design and paired reasoning

slides.title: Complete the changed history policy
body: In faded_practice.py accept only 0, 2, 4 and 6.
Finish append-once saving and test a failed retry.
Run changed rule tests, then the adapted runner.
slides.notes: Use a COPY; complete load_history and save_result without importing lab_rules. Prediction file 2,three,3,6,0 gives[2,6,0] and warnings for lines2 and3; missing/empty gives[]. A finished score6 appends once; a second call leaves file unchanged. Reject odd scores in the changed history policy, even though int conversion succeeds. The save contract assumes a valid score from the game; the loader validates external records. For a failed save, target a disposable directory, check saved=False, then retry with a writable file. Complete practice-tests.csv expected/actual/build evidence. After rule checks use the previously adapted runner; drawing and file I/O remain separate from scoring. Teaching lab and matching workbook: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/index.html#y11-4; https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/workbook.md. slides.strategy: Independent faded task and changed tests

slides.title: When should saved become True?
body: The append raises OSError.
A: Set saved=True before trying to write.
B: Set it only after the write succeeds.
slides.notes: B. A prevents a legitimate retry and falsely claims persistence. Ask learners to distinguish an expected result from an observed file change. The worked runner avoids automatic repeated failures each frame: it attempts once and S retries explicitly. Record the error message without exposing real file paths or student data. Teaching lab and matching workbook: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/index.html#y11-4; https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/workbook.md. Relevant Pygame references: https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/event.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/time.html ; https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/rect.html .

slides.title: Demonstrate and record readiness
body: Show missing, empty and malformed-history cases.
Verify pause, reset, timeout and append-once.
Explain one fresh change without the reference.
slides.notes: Use readiness.csv y11-4 plus the practice test table. Teacher observes one changed rule or test after the independent attempt; copying check_worked_lab output is not evidence of the learner’s own work. Record support, code version, expected/actual, first mismatch, repair and retest. Keep formal practical conditions separate next lesson; this preparation is ungraded. If evidence is incomplete, record targeted reteaching and re-plan before project issue rather than quietly adding workshops. Teaching lab and matching workbook: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/index.html#y11-4; https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/pygame/workbook.md. lessons.title: Controlled practical briefing
lessons.prepare: Teacher supplies the fresh task, permitted resources, assessment conditions, submission location and marking materials separately. Public deck contains process guidance only.

slides.title: Controlled practical briefing
slides.notes: This is the existing Week 7 planner practical slot. Use the teacher-issued task and school assessment arrangements; do not treat this public deck as a complete assessment instrument. Keep the fresh scenario and marking materials in the teacher-controlled distribution channel. Suggested timing is a 55-minute session; adjust to the issued task.
body: Unit 1 · Week 7 · Lesson 4
Apply the skills from Weeks 1–7 to the teacher-issued task.

slides.title: Task and conditions
slides.notes: Issue the fresh problem separately. Confirm permitted resources, collaboration/help rules, time available and what evidence must be submitted. Explain how students can request clarification of wording without receiving a solution. Do not show a worked answer during the controlled attempt. This slide introduces no new marks or weighting.
body: Read the task supplied by your teacher.
Confirm the time and permitted resources.
Check the rules for assistance and collaboration.
Identify the required files and evidence to submit.

slides.title: Requirements before code
slides.notes: Students independently identify required inputs, processing, outputs and data/file formats from the issued brief. They should distinguish task requirements from assumptions and seek permitted clarification. Apply only the features actually required by the task, rather than adding unnecessary file operations or algorithms.
body: Identify the required inputs and outputs.
Note any type, range and file-format rules.
Separate stated requirements from assumptions.
Request permitted clarification of unclear wording.

slides.title: A plan you can explain
slides.notes: Students prepare a brief plan or pseudocode using only conventions/resources allowed in the task. Ask them to decide where selection, repetition, list processing or functions serve the actual problem. They record independent expected results before implementation. Teacher observation follows the issued assessment conditions.
body: Plan the main processing steps.
Choose suitable program structures for the task.
Select tests from the stated requirements.
Calculate expected results before running.

slides.title: Independent implementation
slides.notes: Main implementation interval:20 suggested minutes. Students use the teacher-issued resources and follow its help rules. Teacher handles environment failures in accordance with the task conditions and keeps assessment observations separately. No model code or task-specific answers appear in the public deck.
body: Implement your plan under the issued conditions.
Use clear names and consistent indentation.
Save your work in the required location.
Use the agreed process for technical difficulties.

slides.title: Testing against the requirements
slides.notes: Suggested 10-minute testing interval. Students compare prior expectations with actual results, include applicable normal/boundary/invalid/file cases and record corrections honestly. Which tests are required comes from the issued task. Preserve evidence of a mismatch and rerun rather than replacing expectations to match an error.
body: Compare actual results with your predictions.
Test relevant boundaries and unsuitable input.
Check file contents and repeat runs where required.
Record corrections and rerun the affected tests.

slides.title: Submission check
slides.notes: Allow five suggested minutes for the issued submission procedure. Students verify their own final files open and the requested code/design/test evidence is included. Avoid adding criteria absent from the task. Keep original assessment evidence intact and follow the teacher’s submission directions.
body: Follow the teacher’s submission instructions.
Check the final code and required data files.
Include the requested planning and test evidence.
Confirm the submitted version is the intended version.

slides.title: Reflection after submission
slides.notes: After the controlled attempt ends, students reflect without changing submitted evidence. Teacher decides when task-specific feedback or solutions may be discussed, especially if other classes still need to complete it. Use observations to plan Week 8 design/testing support rather than adding another assessment.
body: Which skill helped you solve the task?
Which test found or prevented a fault?
Name one skill to strengthen next.
Follow your teacher’s directions for later feedback.
